True Statement: Cells of the human body exhibit three main types of movements: amoeboid, ciliary and muscular.
False 1: Cells of the human body exhibit two main types of movements: amoeboid, ciliary and muscular.
FIB 1: Cells of the human body exhibit three main types of movements: ___, ciliary and muscular.
FIB 2: Cells of the human body exhibit three main types of movements: amoeboid, ___ and muscular.
FIB 3: Cells of the human body exhibit three main types of movements: amoeboid, ciliary and ___.
Reason: Amoeboid, ciliary and muscular are structurally and mechanistically distinct movement types; each serves different functions in different cell/tissue contexts.

True Statement: Macrophages and leucocytes in blood exhibit amoeboid movement.
False 1: Macrophages and leucocytes in blood exhibit ciliary movement.
False 2: Macrophages and leucocytes in blood exhibit muscular movement.
FIB 1: ___ and leucocytes in blood exhibit amoeboid movement.
FIB 2: Macrophages and ___ in blood exhibit amoeboid movement.
FIB 3: Macrophages and leucocytes in blood exhibit amoeboid ___.
Reason: Macrophages engulf pathogens by amoeboid movement (pseudopodial extension); leucocytes use it to squeeze through capillary walls into infected tissue.

True Statement: Amoeboid movement is effected by pseudopodia formed by the streaming of protoplasm.
False 1: Ciliary movement is effected by pseudopodia formed by the streaming of protoplasm.
False 2: Flagellar movement is effected by pseudopodia formed by the streaming of protoplasm.
FIB 1: ___ movement is effected by pseudopodia formed by the streaming of protoplasm.
FIB 2: Amoeboid movement is effected by ___ formed by the streaming of protoplasm.
FIB 3: Amoeboid movement is effected by pseudopodia formed by the streaming of ___.
Reason: Pseudopodia form when actin polymerises at the leading edge, pushing the plasma membrane forward; cytoplasm streams into the projection.

True Statement: Cytoskeletal elements like microfilaments are involved in amoeboid movement.
False 1: Cytoskeletal elements like microfilaments are involved in ciliary movement.
False 2: Cytoskeletal elements like microfilaments are involved in muscular movement.
FIB 1: ___ elements like microfilaments are involved in amoeboid movement.
FIB 2: Cytoskeletal elements like ___ are involved in amoeboid movement.
FIB 3: Cytoskeletal elements like microfilaments are involved in amoeboid ___.
Reason: Actin microfilaments are the structural basis of pseudopodium formation; their dynamic polymerisation and depolymerisation drive the streaming movement.

True Statement: Ciliary movement occurs in most of our internal tubular organs which are lined by ciliated epithelium.
False 1: Muscular movement occurs in most of our internal tubular organs which are lined by ciliated epithelium.
FIB 1: ___ movement occurs in most of our internal tubular organs which are lined by ciliated epithelium.
FIB 2: Ciliary movement occurs in most of our internal tubular organs which are lined by ___ epithelium.
FIB 3: Ciliary movement occurs in most of our internal tubular organs which are lined by ciliated ___.
Reason: Internal tubular organs (fallopian tube, trachea) are lined with ciliated epithelium; the coordinated beating of cilia moves materials along the lumen.

True Statement: Coordinated movements of cilia in the trachea help in removing dust particles and foreign substances inhaled with atmospheric air.
False 1: Coordinated movements of flagella in the trachea help in removing dust particles and foreign substances inhaled with atmospheric air.
FIB 1: ___ movements of cilia in the trachea help in removing dust particles and foreign substances inhaled with atmospheric air.
FIB 2: Coordinated movements of cilia in the trachea help in removing dust particles and foreign ___ inhaled with atmospheric air.
FIB 3: Coordinated movements of cilia in the trachea help in removing dust particles and foreign substances inhaled with ___ air.
Reason: Tracheal cilia beat in a coordinated metachronal wave that sweeps mucus (with trapped particles) upward toward the pharynx for removal.

True Statement: Passage of ova through the female reproductive tract is facilitated by ciliary movement.
False 1: Passage of ova through the female reproductive tract is facilitated by muscular movement.
False 2: Passage of ova through the female reproductive tract is facilitated by amoeboid movement.
FIB 1: ___ of ova through the female reproductive tract is facilitated by ciliary movement.
FIB 2: Passage of ova through the female ___ tract is facilitated by ciliary movement.
FIB 3: Passage of ova through the female reproductive tract is ___ by ciliary movement.
Reason: Ovum lacks its own motility; cilia on the fallopian tube epithelium create a current that propels the ovum from the infundibulum toward the uterus.

True Statement: Locomotion requires a perfect coordinated activity of muscular, skeletal and neural systems.
False 1: Locomotion requires a perfect coordinated activity of muscular and skeletal systems only.
FIB 1: ___ requires a perfect coordinated activity of muscular, skeletal and neural systems.
FIB 2: Locomotion requires a perfect ___ activity of muscular, skeletal and neural systems.
FIB 3: Locomotion requires a perfect coordinated activity of muscular, skeletal and neural ___.
Reason: Locomotion is a complex integrated act — muscles provide force, bones provide levers and attachments, and neural circuits coordinate timing and direction.

True Statement: Flagellar movement helps in the swimming of spermatozoa, maintenance of water current in the canal system of sponges, and in locomotion of Protists like Euglena.
False 1: Ciliary movement helps in the swimming of spermatozoa, maintenance of water current in the canal system of sponges, and in locomotion of Protists like Euglena.
False 2: Amoeboid movement helps in the swimming of spermatozoa, maintenance of water current in the canal system of sponges, and in locomotion of Protists like Euglena.
FIB 1: Flagellar movement helps in the swimming of spermatozoa, maintenance of water current in the canal system of sponges, and in ___ of Protists like Euglena.
FIB 2: Flagellar movement helps in the swimming of spermatozoa, maintenance of water current in the canal system of sponges, and in locomotion of ___ like Euglena.
FIB 3: Flagellar movement helps in the swimming of spermatozoa, maintenance of water current in the canal system of sponges, and in locomotion of Protists like ___.
Reason: Flagella are longer than cilia and produce a whip-like motion; spermatozoa are propelled by the flagellar axoneme powered by dynein ATPase.

True Statement: Muscle is a specialised tissue of mesodermal origin.
False 1: Muscle is a specialised tissue of ectodermal origin.
False 2: Muscle is a specialised tissue of endodermal origin.
FIB 1: ___ is a specialised tissue of mesodermal origin.
FIB 2: Muscle is a ___ tissue of mesodermal origin.
FIB 3: Muscle is a specialised tissue of ___ origin.
Reason: Mesoderm gives rise to muscles, bones, kidneys, the dermis, and the cardiovascular system; ectoderm gives skin epidermis and nerve tissue.

True Statement: About 40–50 per cent of the body weight of a human adult is contributed by muscles.
False 1: About 20–30 per cent of the body weight of a human adult is contributed by muscles.
False 2: About 60–70 per cent of the body weight of a human adult is contributed by muscles.
FIB 1: About ___ per cent of the body weight of a human adult is contributed by muscles.
FIB 2: About 40–50 per cent of the body weight of a human adult is ___ by muscles.
FIB 3: About 40–50 per cent of the body weight of a human adult is contributed by ___.
Reason: Muscles account for 40–50% body mass because a large number of skeletal fibres are needed for locomotion, posture and heat generation.

True Statement: Muscles have special properties: excitability, contractility, extensibility and elasticity.
False 1: Muscles have special properties: excitability and contractility only.
FIB 1: Muscles have special properties: excitability, ___, extensibility and elasticity.
FIB 2: Muscles have special properties: excitability, contractility, ___ and elasticity.
FIB 3: Muscles have special properties: excitability, contractility, extensibility and ___.
Reason: Excitability allows muscles to respond to signals; contractility shortens the fibre; extensibility allows lengthening; elasticity returns the fibre to resting length.

True Statement: Based on location, three types of muscles are identified: skeletal, visceral and cardiac.
False 1: Based on location, two types of muscles are identified: skeletal, visceral and cardiac.
FIB 1: Based on location, three types of muscles are ___: skeletal, visceral and cardiac.
FIB 2: Based on location, three types of muscles are identified: skeletal, ___ and cardiac.
FIB 3: Based on location, three types of muscles are identified: skeletal, visceral and ___.
Reason: Muscle location determines its control (voluntary/involuntary), structure (striated/non-striated) and function (locomotion/organ movement/pumping blood).

True Statement: Skeletal muscles have a striped (striated) appearance and are voluntary muscles primarily involved in locomotory actions.
False 1: Skeletal muscles have a non-striated (smooth) appearance and are involuntary muscles.
False 2: Visceral muscles have a striped (striated) appearance and are voluntary muscles primarily involved in locomotory actions.
FIB 1: ___ muscles have a striped (striated) appearance and are voluntary muscles primarily involved in locomotory actions.
FIB 2: Skeletal muscles have a striped (striated) ___ and are voluntary muscles primarily involved in locomotory actions.
FIB 3: Skeletal muscles have a striped (striated) appearance and are voluntary muscles primarily involved in ___ actions.
Reason: Striated appearance reflects the regular alternation of thick (myosin) and thin (actin) filament arrays; voluntary control reflects their somatic motor innervation.

True Statement: Visceral muscles are smooth (nonstriated) and involuntary, located in the inner walls of hollow visceral organs.
False 1: Visceral muscles are striated and voluntary, located in the inner walls of hollow visceral organs.
False 2: Skeletal muscles are smooth (nonstriated) and involuntary, located in the inner walls of hollow visceral organs.
FIB 1: ___ muscles are smooth (nonstriated) and involuntary, located in the inner walls of hollow visceral organs.
FIB 2: Visceral muscles are smooth (___) and involuntary, located in the inner walls of hollow visceral organs.
FIB 3: Visceral muscles are smooth (nonstriated) and ___, located in the inner walls of hollow visceral organs.
Reason: Visceral smooth muscle lacks Z-lines and has no regular filament arrays, giving a smooth appearance; it is controlled by the autonomic nervous system.

True Statement: Cardiac muscles are striated, branched and involuntary.
False 1: Cardiac muscles are non-striated, unbranched and voluntary.
False 2: Cardiac muscles are striated, branched and voluntary.
False 3: Visceral muscles are striated, branched and involuntary.
FIB 1: ___ muscles are striated, branched and involuntary.
FIB 2: Cardiac muscles are striated, ___ and involuntary.
FIB 3: Cardiac muscles are striated, branched and ___.
Reason: Cardiac muscle is striated (like skeletal) to generate strong contractions but is branched (intercalated discs) and involuntary for continuous rhythmic pumping.

True Statement: Each organised skeletal muscle is made of muscle bundles (fascicles) held together by a collagenous connective tissue layer called fascia.
False 1: Each organised skeletal muscle is made of muscle bundles (fascicles) held together by an elastic connective tissue layer called fascia.
FIB 1: Each organised skeletal muscle is made of muscle bundles (fascicles) held ___ by a collagenous connective tissue layer called fascia.
FIB 2: Each organised skeletal muscle is made of muscle bundles (fascicles) held together by a ___ connective tissue layer called fascia.
FIB 3: Each organised skeletal muscle is made of muscle bundles (fascicles) held together by a collagenous ___ tissue layer called fascia.
Reason: Fascia (collagenous connective tissue) holds muscle bundles together and transmits force from fibres to tendons; collagen provides tensile strength.

True Statement: Each muscle bundle contains a number of muscle fibres.
False 1: Each muscle bundle contains a single muscle fibre.
FIB 1: Each muscle bundle ___ a number of muscle fibres.
FIB 2: Each muscle bundle contains a number of ___ fibres.
FIB 3: Each muscle bundle contains a number of muscle ___.
Reason: Each bundle (fascicle) is surrounded by perimysium; the entire muscle is surrounded by epimysium; individual fibres are surrounded by endomysium.

True Statement: Each muscle fibre is lined by the plasma membrane called sarcolemma.
False 1: Each muscle fibre is lined by the plasma membrane called sarcoplasm.
FIB 1: Each muscle fibre is lined by the plasma ___ called sarcolemma.
FIB 2: Each muscle fibre is lined by the plasma membrane ___ sarcolemma.
FIB 3: Each muscle fibre is lined by the plasma membrane called ___.
Reason: Sarcolemma is the specialised plasma membrane of the muscle fibre; it propagates the action potential along the fibre and into the T-tubule network.

True Statement: Muscle fibre is a syncytium as the sarcoplasm contains many nuclei.
False 1: Muscle fibre is a syncytium as the sarcoplasm contains a single nucleus.
False 2: Muscle fibre is a syncytium as the sarcolemma contains many nuclei.
FIB 1: Muscle fibre is a ___ as the sarcoplasm contains many nuclei.
FIB 2: Muscle fibre is a syncytium as the ___ contains many nuclei.
FIB 3: Muscle fibre is a syncytium as the sarcoplasm ___ many nuclei.
Reason: Skeletal muscle fibres form by fusion of many myoblasts during development (syncytium = multiple nuclei in one continuous cytoplasm); many nuclei direct the high metabolic activity.

True Statement: The sarcoplasmic reticulum of the muscle fibres is the storehouse of calcium ions.
False 1: The sarcoplasmic reticulum of the muscle fibres is the storehouse of sodium ions.
False 2: The sarcoplasm of the muscle fibres is the storehouse of calcium ions.
False 3: The sarcoplasmic reticulum of the muscle fibres is the storehouse of potassium ions.
FIB 1: The ___ reticulum of the muscle fibres is the storehouse of calcium ions.
FIB 2: The sarcoplasmic reticulum of the muscle fibres is the ___ of calcium ions.
FIB 3: The sarcoplasmic reticulum of the muscle fibres is the storehouse of ___ ions.
Reason: Sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) surrounds each myofibril; it stores Ca²⁺ and releases it when the action potential arrives, triggering contraction.

True Statement: A large number of parallelly arranged filaments in the sarcoplasm called myofilaments or myofibrils are a characteristic feature of the muscle fibre.
False 1: A large number of parallelly arranged filaments in the sarcolemma called myofilaments or myofibrils are a characteristic feature of the muscle fibre.
FIB 1: A large number of parallelly arranged filaments in the sarcoplasm called ___ or myofibrils are a characteristic feature of the muscle fibre.
FIB 2: A large number of parallelly arranged filaments in the sarcoplasm called myofilaments or ___ are a characteristic feature of the muscle fibre.
FIB 3: A large number of parallelly arranged filaments in the sarcoplasm called myofilaments or myofibrils are a ___ feature of the muscle fibre.
Reason: Thousands of parallel myofibrils align precisely within the fibre; their regular arrangement of thick and thin filaments creates the characteristic striped pattern.

True Statement: The striated appearance of muscle fibres is due to the distribution pattern of two proteins — Actin and Myosin.
False 1: The striated appearance of muscle fibres is due to the distribution pattern of two proteins — Troponin and Tropomyosin.
FIB 1: The striated appearance of muscle fibres is due to the ___ pattern of two proteins — Actin and Myosin.
FIB 2: The striated appearance of muscle fibres is due to the distribution pattern of two proteins — ___ and Myosin.
FIB 3: The striated appearance of muscle fibres is due to the distribution pattern of two proteins — Actin and ___.
Reason: Actin (thin filaments) is relatively transparent to polarised light (isotropic) → light band (I-band); myosin (thick filaments) rotates the plane of light (anisotropic) → dark band (A-band).

True Statement: The light bands (I-band / Isotropic band) contain actin.
False 1: The light bands (I-band / Isotropic band) contain myosin.
False 2: The dark bands (A-band / Anisotropic band) contain actin.
FIB 1: The light bands (I-band / ___ band) contain actin.
FIB 2: The light bands (I-band / Isotropic band) ___ actin.
FIB 3: The light bands (I-band / Isotropic band) contain ___.
Reason: The I-band (Isotropic band) contains only thin actin filaments with no overlapping thick filaments; being less optically dense it appears light under polarised light.

True Statement: The dark band (A-band / Anisotropic band) contains myosin.
False 1: The dark band (A-band / Anisotropic band) contains actin.
False 2: The light band (I-band / Isotropic band) contains myosin.
FIB 1: The dark band (A-band / ___ band) contains myosin.
FIB 2: The dark band (A-band / Anisotropic band) ___ myosin.
FIB 3: The dark band (A-band / Anisotropic band) contains ___.
Reason: Myosin thick filaments form the dense A-band; they are anchored at the M-line and extend to where they overlap with actin in both directions.

True Statement: Actin filaments are thinner (thin filaments) and myosin filaments are thicker (thick filaments).
False 1: Actin filaments are thicker (thick filaments) and myosin filaments are thinner (thin filaments).
FIB 1: Actin filaments are ___ (thin filaments) and myosin filaments are thicker (thick filaments).
FIB 2: Actin filaments are thinner (thin filaments) and myosin filaments are ___ (thick filaments).
FIB 3: Actin filaments are thinner (thin filaments) and myosin filaments are thicker (thick ___).
Reason: Actin is thinner (7 nm) and myosin is thicker (15 nm); thicker filaments produce the darker (A) band and thinner filaments produce the lighter (I) band.

True Statement: In the centre of each I-band is an elastic fibre called Z-line which bisects it.
False 1: In the centre of each A-band is an elastic fibre called Z-line which bisects it.
False 2: In the centre of each I-band is an elastic fibre called M-line which bisects it.
FIB 1: In the centre of each ___ is an elastic fibre called Z-line which bisects it.
FIB 2: In the centre of each I-band is an elastic fibre called ___ which bisects it.
FIB 3: In the centre of each I-band is an elastic fibre called Z-line which ___ it.
Reason: Z-line (from German 'Zwischenscheibe' = intermediate disc) anchors the thin actin filaments and defines the boundaries of each sarcomere.

True Statement: The thin filaments are firmly attached to the Z-line.
False 1: The thin filaments are firmly attached to the M-line.
False 2: The thick filaments are firmly attached to the Z-line.
FIB 1: The thin ___ are firmly attached to the Z-line.
FIB 2: The thin filaments are firmly ___ to the Z-line.
FIB 3: The thin filaments are firmly attached to the ___.
Reason: Thin filaments are cross-linked to the Z-line by α-actinin; this ensures that when myosin pulls them inward, the entire Z-line and sarcomere shorten.

True Statement: The thick filaments in the A-band are held together in the middle by a thin fibrous membrane called M-line.
False 1: The thick filaments in the A-band are held together in the middle by a thin fibrous membrane called Z-line.
False 2: The thin filaments in the I-band are held together in the middle by a thin fibrous membrane called M-line.
False 3: The thick filaments in the I-band are held together in the middle by a thin fibrous membrane called M-line.
FIB 1: The thick filaments in the ___ are held together in the middle by a thin fibrous membrane called M-line.
FIB 2: The thick filaments in the A-band are held together in the middle by a thin fibrous ___ called M-line.
FIB 3: The thick filaments in the A-band are held together in the middle by a thin fibrous membrane called ___.
Reason: M-line proteins (myomesin, M-protein) crosslink adjacent myosin thick filaments to maintain their precise hexagonal spacing during contraction.

True Statement: The sarcomere is the portion of the myofibril between two successive Z-lines and is the functional unit of contraction.
False 1: The sarcomere is the portion of the myofibril between two successive M-lines and is the functional unit of contraction.
False 2: The myofibril is the portion between two successive Z-lines and is the functional unit of contraction.
False 3: The sarcomere is the portion of the myofibril between two successive Z-lines and is the functional unit of relaxation.
FIB 1: The sarcomere is the portion of the myofibril between two successive ___ and is the functional unit of contraction.
FIB 2: The sarcomere is the portion of the myofibril between two successive Z-lines and is the ___ unit of contraction.
FIB 3: The sarcomere is the portion of the myofibril between two successive Z-lines and is the functional unit of ___.
Reason: One sarcomere = Z-line to Z-line; it is the minimal unit that contains the full complement of thick and thin filaments and can shorten independently.

True Statement: In the resting state, the central part of the thick filament not overlapped by thin filaments is called the H-zone.
False 1: In the resting state, the central part of the thin filament not overlapped by thick filaments is called the H-zone.
False 2: In the resting state, the central part of the thick filament not overlapped by thin filaments is called the Z-zone.
False 3: In the resting state, the central part of the thick filament not overlapped by thin filaments is called the M-zone.
FIB 1: In the resting state, the central part of the thick filament not ___ by thin filaments is called the H-zone.
FIB 2: In the resting state, the central part of the thick filament not overlapped by thin ___ is called the H-zone.
FIB 3: In the resting state, the central part of the thick filament not overlapped by thin filaments is called the ___.
Reason: In the resting state, thin filaments do not reach the centre of the A-band; the H-zone is the bare shaft of thick filament with no thin filament overlap.

True Statement: Each actin (thin) filament is made of two F-actins helically wound to each other.
False 1: Each actin (thin) filament is made of three F-actins helically wound to each other.
False 2: Each actin (thin) filament is made of two G-actins helically wound to each other.
FIB 1: Each actin (thin) ___ is made of two F-actins helically wound to each other.
FIB 2: Each actin (thin) filament is made of two ___ helically wound to each other.
FIB 3: Each actin (thin) filament is made of two F-actins ___ wound to each other.
Reason: Two F-actin (filamentous actin) polymers wind around each other in a right-handed helix; the double helix gives the thin filament structural stability.

True Statement: Each F-actin is a polymer of monomeric G-actins.
False 1: Each G-actin is a polymer of monomeric F-actins.
False 2: Each F-actin is a monomer of polymeric G-actins.
FIB 1: Each ___ is a polymer of monomeric G-actins.
FIB 2: Each F-actin is a polymer of ___ G-actins.
FIB 3: Each F-actin is a polymer of monomeric ___.
Reason: F-actin (filamentous) is the polymer; G-actin (globular) is the monomer; ATP-G-actin polymerises to form the helical F-actin strand.

True Statement: Two filaments of tropomyosin run close to the F-actins throughout their length.
False 1: One filament of tropomyosin runs close to the F-actins throughout their length.
False 2: Two filaments of troponin run close to the F-actins throughout their length.
FIB 1: Two filaments of ___ run close to the F-actins throughout their length.
FIB 2: Two filaments of tropomyosin run close to the ___ throughout their length.
FIB 3: Two filaments of tropomyosin run close to the F-actins ___ their length.
Reason: Two tropomyosin strands lie in the grooves of the actin double helix; at rest, tropomyosin blocks the myosin-binding sites on actin.

True Statement: Troponin is distributed at regular intervals on the tropomyosin.
False 1: Tropomyosin is distributed at regular intervals on the troponin.
False 2: Troponin is distributed at irregular intervals on the tropomyosin.
FIB 1: ___ is distributed at regular intervals on the tropomyosin.
FIB 2: Troponin is ___ at regular intervals on the tropomyosin.
FIB 3: Troponin is distributed at regular intervals on the ___.
Reason: Troponin complex (TnT, TnI, TnC) is placed at regular intervals (every 7 G-actin subunits) along tropomyosin; TnC binds Ca²⁺ to trigger contraction.

True Statement: In the resting state, a subunit of troponin masks the active binding sites for myosin on the actin filaments.
False 1: In the resting state, a subunit of tropomyosin masks the active binding sites for myosin on the actin filaments.
False 2: In the resting state, a subunit of troponin masks the active binding sites for actin on the myosin filaments.
FIB 1: In the resting state, a subunit of ___ masks the active binding sites for myosin on the actin filaments.
FIB 2: In the resting state, a subunit of troponin masks the active ___ sites for myosin on the actin filaments.
FIB 3: In the resting state, a subunit of troponin masks the active binding sites for myosin on the actin ___.
Reason: In the resting state, troponin holds tropomyosin over the actin binding sites; this prevents cross-bridge formation and keeps the muscle relaxed.

True Statement: Each myosin (thick) filament is a polymerised protein made of many monomeric proteins called Meromyosins.
False 1: Each myosin (thick) filament is a polymerised protein made of many monomeric proteins called Tropomyosins.
False 2: Each myosin (thick) filament is a polymerised protein made of many dimeric proteins called Meromyosins.
FIB 1: Each myosin (thick) filament is a ___ protein made of many monomeric proteins called Meromyosins.
FIB 2: Each myosin (thick) filament is a polymerised protein made of many monomeric ___ called Meromyosins.
FIB 3: Each myosin (thick) filament is a polymerised protein made of many monomeric proteins called ___.
Reason: Each thick filament is a bundle of ~300 myosin molecules packed tail-to-tail; their heads project outward to form cross-bridges with actin.

True Statement: Each meromyosin has a globular head with a short arm (heavy meromyosin, HMM) and a tail (light meromyosin, LMM).
False 1: Each meromyosin has a globular head with a short arm (light meromyosin, LMM) and a tail (heavy meromyosin, HMM).
FIB 1: Each meromyosin has a globular head with a short arm (heavy meromyosin, ___) and a tail (light meromyosin, LMM).
FIB 2: Each meromyosin has a globular head with a short arm (heavy meromyosin, HMM) and a tail (light ___, LMM).
FIB 3: Each meromyosin has a globular head with a short arm (heavy meromyosin, HMM) and a tail (light meromyosin, ___).
Reason: HMM (heavy meromyosin) = S1 (globular head) + S2 (short arm); LMM (light meromyosin) = the tail that forms the filament backbone.

True Statement: The HMM component (head and short arm) projects outwards at regular distance and angle from the myosin filament surface and is known as the cross arm.
False 1: The LMM component (tail) projects outwards at regular distance and angle from the myosin filament surface and is known as the cross arm.
False 2: The HMM component projects outwards at irregular distance and angle from the myosin filament surface and is known as the cross arm.
FIB 1: The ___ component (head and short arm) projects outwards at regular distance and angle from the myosin filament surface and is known as the cross arm.
FIB 2: The HMM component (head and short arm) projects outwards at regular distance and angle from the myosin ___ surface and is known as the cross arm.
FIB 3: The HMM component (head and short arm) projects outwards at regular distance and angle from the myosin filament ___ and is known as the cross arm.
Reason: Cross arms (HMM) project radially from the filament; they bridge the gap between thick and thin filaments and move thin filaments during contraction.

True Statement: The globular head is an active ATPase enzyme and has binding sites for ATP and active sites for actin.
False 1: The globular head is an active ATPase enzyme and has binding sites for ADP and active sites for actin.
False 2: The globular head is an active ATPase enzyme and has binding sites for ATP and active sites for myosin.
FIB 1: The globular head is an active ___ enzyme and has binding sites for ATP and active sites for actin.
FIB 2: The globular head is an active ATPase enzyme and has ___ sites for ATP and active sites for actin.
FIB 3: The globular head is an active ATPase enzyme and has binding sites for ___ and active sites for actin.
Reason: The globular head contains both the ATPase activity (to hydrolyse ATP for energy) and the actin-binding site (to form the cross-bridge).

True Statement: The sliding filament theory states that contraction of a muscle fibre takes place by the sliding of the thin filaments over the thick filaments.
False 1: The sliding filament theory states that contraction of a muscle fibre takes place by the sliding of the thick filaments over the thin filaments.
FIB 1: The sliding filament theory states that ___ of a muscle fibre takes place by the sliding of the thin filaments over the thick filaments.
FIB 2: The sliding filament theory states that contraction of a muscle fibre takes place by the ___ of the thin filaments over the thick filaments.
FIB 3: The sliding filament theory states that contraction of a muscle fibre takes place by the sliding of the thin filaments over the thick ___.
Reason: During contraction, thin filaments slide over thick filaments toward the A-band centre; the filaments themselves do not shorten — the sarcomere shortens because thin filaments are pulled inward.

True Statement: Muscle contraction is initiated by a signal sent by the central nervous system (CNS) via a motor neuron.
False 1: Muscle contraction is initiated by a signal sent by the central nervous system (CNS) via a sensory neuron.
False 2: Muscle contraction is initiated by a signal sent by the peripheral nervous system (PNS) via a motor neuron.
FIB 1: Muscle ___ is initiated by a signal sent by the central nervous system (CNS) via a motor neuron.
FIB 2: Muscle contraction is initiated by a signal sent by the ___ nervous system (CNS) via a motor neuron.
FIB 3: Muscle contraction is initiated by a signal sent by the central ___ system (CNS) via a motor neuron.
Reason: The CNS sends a voluntary action potential down the motor nerve to initiate a controlled contraction; sensory neurons carry information back from muscles.

True Statement: A motor unit consists of a motor neuron and the muscle fibres connected to it.
False 1: A motor unit consists of a sensory neuron and the muscle fibres connected to it.
FIB 1: A motor unit ___ of a motor neuron and the muscle fibres connected to it.
FIB 2: A motor unit consists of a motor neuron and the muscle ___ connected to it.
FIB 3: A motor unit consists of a motor neuron and the muscle fibres ___ to it.
Reason: One motor neuron innervates multiple muscle fibres; they all contract together (motor unit) when the neuron fires, allowing graded force by recruitment.

True Statement: The junction between a motor neuron and the sarcolemma of the muscle fibre is called the neuromuscular junction or motor-end plate.
False 1: The junction between a sensory neuron and the sarcolemma of the muscle fibre is called the neuromuscular junction or motor-end plate.
False 2: The junction between a motor neuron and the sarcoplasm of the muscle fibre is called the neuromuscular junction or motor-end plate.
FIB 1: The junction between a motor neuron and the ___ of the muscle fibre is called the neuromuscular junction or motor-end plate.
FIB 2: The junction between a motor neuron and the sarcolemma of the muscle fibre is called the ___ junction or motor-end plate.
FIB 3: The junction between a motor neuron and the sarcolemma of the muscle fibre is called the neuromuscular junction or ___ plate.
Reason: The neuromuscular junction (NMJ) is where the motor nerve terminal and the muscle sarcolemma interact; ACh is released from synaptic vesicles here.

True Statement: A neural signal at the neuromuscular junction releases a neurotransmitter (Acetylcholine) which generates an action potential in the sarcolemma.
False 1: A neural signal at the neuromuscular junction releases a neurotransmitter (Acetylcholine) which generates an action potential in the sarcoplasm.
FIB 1: A neural signal at the neuromuscular junction releases a ___ (Acetylcholine) which generates an action potential in the sarcolemma.
